corinthians2.11.p1.b1.text: I hope you will bear with a little of my foolishness, but you are already doing that.

corinthians2.11.p1.b2.text: I am jealous for you with a godly jealousy. For I promised you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ.

corinthians2.11.p1.b3.text: I am afraid, however, that … your minds may be led astray from your simple and pure devotion to Christ.

corinthians2.11.p1.b4.text: Although I am not a polished speaker, I am certainly not lacking in knowledge.

corinthians2.11.p2.b1.text: Was it a sin for me to humble myself in order to exalt you, because I preached the gospel of God to you free of charge?

corinthians2.11.p2.b2.text: And when I was with you and in need, I was not a burden to anyone…

corinthians2.11.p2.b3.text: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do!

corinthians2.11.p3.b1.text: But I will keep on doing what I am doing, in order to undercut those who want an opportunity…

corinthians2.11.p3.b2.text: For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, masquerading as apostles of Christ.

corinthians2.11.p3.b3.text: And no wonder, for Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light.

corinthians2.11.p3.b4.text: …Their end will correspond to their actions.

corinthians2.11.p4.b1.text: I repeat: Let no one take me for a fool. But if you do, then receive me as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.

corinthians2.11.p4.b2.text: For you gladly tolerate fools, since you are so wise.

corinthians2.11.p4.b3.text: …Speaking as a fool, however, I can match what anyone else dares to boast about.

corinthians2.11.p5.b1.text: Are they Hebrews? So am I.

corinthians2.11.p5.b2.text: Are they Israelites? So am I.

corinthians2.11.p5.b3.text: Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.

corinthians2.11.p5.b4.text: Are they servants of Christ? I am speaking like I am out of my mind, but I am so much more: in harder labor, in more imprisonments…

corinthians2.11.p6.b1.text: Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one.

corinthians2.11.p6.b2.text: Three times I was beaten with rods…

corinthians2.11.p7.b1.text: …three times I was shipwrecked. I spent a night and a day in the open sea.

corinthians2.11.p7.b2.text: In my frequent journeys, I have been in danger from rivers and from bandits, in danger from my countrymen and from the Gentiles…

corinthians2.11.p7.b3.text: …in danger in the city and in the country, in danger on the sea and among false brothers…

corinthians2.11.p8.b1.text: in labor and toil and often without sleep, in hunger and thirst and often without food, in cold and exposure.

corinthians2.11.p8.b2.text: Apart from these external trials, I face daily the pressure of my concern for all the churches.

corinthians2.11.p8.b3.text: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is led into sin, and I do not burn with grief?

corinthians2.11.p9.b1.text: If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness.

corinthians2.11.p9.b2.text: But I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall and escaped his grasp.
